name: browser.loginlogin
description:
Sign in on the current site through the login agent.

Start it whenever the task needs a sign-in, whether or not a saved login exists: when none fits, the <!-- personal-muse-only:start -->user<!-- personal-muse-only:end --><!-- group-muse-only:start -->group<!-- group-muse-only:end --> gets a secure entry <!-- personal-muse-only:start -->card<!-- personal-muse-only:end --><!-- group-muse-only:start -->link<!-- group-muse-only:end -->. Name the tab and describe the sign-in needed, the current step, and any account choice or relevant previous attempt. Add `account_hint` only when your assignment identifies the account. When your assignment asks for <!-- personal-muse-only:start -->the user's<!-- personal-muse-only:end --><!-- group-muse-only:start -->a member's<!-- group-muse-only:end --> approval before a one-time code is used, or says to stop at a code step for it, tell the login agent only that <!-- personal-muse-only:start -->the user approves<!-- personal-muse-only:end --><!-- group-muse-only:start -->members approve<!-- group-muse-only:end --> codes before use: its code step puts every code fetched for it <!-- personal-muse-only:start -->on the user's approval card<!-- personal-muse-only:end --><!-- group-muse-only:start -->to an approval in the group<!-- group-muse-only:end --> before it goes in, and that is the approval<!-- personal-muse-only:start -->. Tell it to stop at a code step only when your assignment says the user enters codes themselves<!-- personal-muse-only:end -->. The login agent confirms an existing sign-in or completes the site's sign-in: the credential service obtains consent and enters saved usernames and passwords without revealing them, and the login service enters the one-time codes for the login agent's code steps, from the <!-- personal-muse-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-muse-only:end --><!-- group-muse-only:start -->group's connected<!-- group-muse-only:end --> mail or from the main agent. Account choices the main agent sends reach the login agent through the runtime, and so do the codes the main agent sends as answers to its questions. A code the main agent sends while no login agent works on its site comes to you as a note; give it to the login agent with `browser.steer_specialist`, or start one with it in the instruction. A successful result names the signed-in account; a sign-in that stops short names the site. Copy that site exactly into `browser.report`.

Called by the browser agent, the call starts the login agent as a specialist and returns at once with its ID. You can still act on its tab, but that can undo its progress, so work on other tabs meanwhile. The runtime delivers its result to you automatically as a handoff message when it finishes. Do not poll or sleep to wait for it. Calls from the checkout agent wait for the login agent's result. After a blocked result, start the login agent again once when the result says what to change, such as another account, method or sign-in page; after a second blocked result, report it. Report a `needs_input` result as it came, with its need and its `reason`.
